subject: Art of Teaching
explanation:
A student-centric classroom puts learners at the centre of planning and activities. Because students differ in ability, pace, interest and learning style, the approach is mainly meant to address individual differences through varied tasks, choices and group work.
- Reducing teacher-oriented lectures is a result of the approach rather than its purpose.
- Recalling previous knowledge is a lesson-step.
- Engaging the entire class is desirable, but is not what is distinctive about student-centred teaching.
Hence option A is the best answer.

subject: Art of Teaching
explanation:
Teacher training prepares teachers for the profession in several ways. It increases teaching skills such as questioning, explaining and classroom management; it makes them understand how a school is organised and run; and it updates their knowledge of the content they teach, along with pedagogy.
Because each of the options A, B and C is a valid reason, 'All these' is the correct choice.

subject: Art of Teaching
explanation:
Audio-visual aids engage both hearing and sight. Television shows moving pictures with sound, so it is a standard audio-visual aid.
- Radio is an audio-only aid.
- A museum is a community resource or visual/real-object source for learning, and is generally not classed as an audio-visual device.
- Hence 'TV and Museum' is also not correct.
The key is therefore option A, television. The classification of radio as audio-only is conventional.

subject: Art of Teaching
explanation:
Multimedia combines audio, video, images and text, so it engages several senses at once. Learning through more than one sense improves attention, understanding and retention, which explains why the first section grasped the parts of a plant better than students who saw only a blackboard diagram.
- Brightness of students is an unsupported assumption.
- The blackboard is a useful visual aid, so B is incorrect.
- Cost is not the reason for better understanding.

subject: General Knowledge
concept: Name given by Udham Singh to police
explanation:
After shooting Michael O'Dwyer in London in 1940, Udham Singh is recorded as giving his name as Ram Mohammad Singh Azad, a name that combined the major religions of India and symbolised anti-colonial unity. Among the options, 'Mohammed Singh Azad' is the closest form, as 'Ram Singh' and 'Azad' alone are incomplete.
The option text omits 'Ram', so it is not exact, but D is the best available answer and matches the key.

subject: General Knowledge
concept: India's rank in water availability per person
keyNote: This is a recall item from a textbook statistic; I could not verify it independently.
explanation:
This looks like a textbook statement (NCERT-type material on water resources) that India ranks 133rd in the world in terms of water availability per person per annum. The other options (135, 17, 98) do not match that statement.
The figure depends on the source and year used, so I could not verify it independently and my confidence is low, but 133 is the value that matches the commonly quoted statement and the key.

subject: General Knowledge
concept: Federalism divides power between centre and units
explanation:
Federalism is a system of government in which power is divided between a central authority and the constituent units, such as states or provinces, each of which has its own sphere of authority. The stem already names the constituent units, so the missing word is the central authority.
- B (states) repeats the 'constituent units' already mentioned.
- C (both) would repeat the units again.
Hence option A is the correct completion.

subject: General Knowledge
concept: Founder of Bihar Provincial Kisan Sabha
explanation: The Bihar Provincial Kisan Sabha was formed in 1929 at Sonepur by Swami Sahajanand Saraswati, who later led the peasant movement in Bihar and became president of the All India Kisan Sabha (1936). The other names are also linked with Bihar's politics, but they are not credited with founding the Kisan Sabha. This is a frequently asked Bihar history fact: Sahajanand's peasant organisation later grew into a national body and fought against zamindari exploitation and illegal levies on tenants.

subject: General Knowledge
concept: Author of Gandhi and Bihar reminiscences
explanation:
The book 'Mahatma Gandhi and Bihar: Some Reminiscences' was written by Dr. Rajendra Prasad, the first President of India, who was closely associated with Gandhi from the Champaran Satyagraha (1917) onwards. His other works include 'Satyagraha at Champaran' and 'India Divided'.
J. P. Narayan, Karpoori Thakur and Ramavriksha Benipuri are Bihar leaders or writers but are not known as the author of this title.

subject: General Knowledge
explanation: Recreation means activities done in leisure time for enjoyment and relaxation. Painting, listening to music and reading a book are all pursued for pleasure and renewal, so all of them are recreational activities. Since each of A, B and C qualifies, the correct option is 'All of these'. The remaining part of the idea is that recreation is a wide category, so no single listed activity is the only correct choice, and this is why the combined option is right.

subject: General Knowledge
explanation:
A postman delivers letters, a cobbler mends shoes and a nurse treats the sick, so options A, B and D are correct matches. Maintaining law and order is the job of the police, not of a teacher, who teaches and guides students.
The incorrect match is therefore option C. So in the list, the teacher's duty is teaching, and the mismatch is easy to spot by comparing each person with the main duty given.

subject: Environmental Science
explanation:
Check each pair:
- Iron deficiency causes anaemia: correct.
- Vitamin B5 (pantothenic acid) is not linked to pellagra; pellagra is caused by a lack of vitamin B3 (niacin): incorrect.
- Vitamin B3 is niacin: correct.
- Vitamin K helps in blood clotting: correct.
So the pair that is incorrectly matched is option B. Remember the standard vitamin-deficiency pairs: B1 beriberi, B3 pellagra, C scurvy, D rickets, A night blindness.

subject: Environmental Science
explanation:
A drought is a prolonged period of deficient or irregular rainfall that leads to water scarcity and crop failure.
- Cyclone: a violent storm system with strong winds and rain.
- Earthquake: shaking caused by movement of the Earth's crust.
- Tsunami: giant sea waves, usually from undersea earthquakes.
Only droughts result from scarce or irregularly distributed rain. Droughts are usually classified as meteorological (low rainfall), agricultural and hydrological types, all starting from rainfall deficiency.

subject: General Knowledge
concept: Port nearest to Rourkela Steel Plant
explanation:
Rourkela Steel Plant is in Odisha. Of the listed ports, Paradip (Odisha) is the closest, at roughly 400 km by rail and road, and handles shipments for Odisha's industrial belt.
- Haldia (West Bengal) is farther away.
- Visakhapatnam (Andhra Pradesh) is farther again.
- Kandla is in Gujarat on the west coast, very far.
So Paradip is the nearest port.

subject: Mathematical Aptitude
explanation:
A radish is a root vegetable that is wide near the top and tapers to a point at the bottom, which is the shape of a cone. A cube has square faces, a circle is a flat two-dimensional figure and a cylinder has equal circular ends, so none of these describes a tapering root.
The answer therefore is cone, option C, which matches the key. Some radish varieties are cylindrical, but the textbook shape is a cone.

subject: Mathematical Aptitude
explanation:
A sphere has one continuous curved surface, with no flat faces, no edges and no vertices (corners). In primary mathematics textbooks this single curved surface is counted as one face.
- Vertex: a sphere has none.
- Edge: a sphere has none.
So 'face' is the only item that applies with a count of one, so option A is correct. Some books say a sphere has 'no faces', so the wording is textbook-dependent.

subject: Mathematical Aptitude
concept: Forming a number from place values
explanation: Write the digits by place: thousands = 8, hundreds = not given (0), tens = 4, units = 2. The number is 8000 + 0 + 40 + 2 = 8042. Check the options: 2048 has thousands digit 2; 8402 has tens digit 0 and hundreds 4; 2408 has thousands 2. Only 8042 fits, so the answer is B. Reading the place values carefully is the key: the hundreds place is not mentioned, so it must be zero, not any other digit.

subject: Mathematical Aptitude
explanation:
Convert each fraction to a decimal:
- 2/10 = 0.2
- 3/100 = 0.03
- 4/1000 = 0.004
Add them: 0.2 + 0.03 + 0.004 = 0.234. The other options are not close to this value, so the answer is 0.234, option B. Because the denominators are powers of ten, each fraction converts directly to a decimal place: tenths, hundredths and thousandths, so no common denominator is needed. Using a common denominator of 1000 also gives (200 + 30 + 4)/1000 = 234/1000.

subject: Logical Reasoning
explanation: Tomato, brinjal and lady finger are fruit vegetables, that is, the fruit of the plant is eaten. Radish is a root vegetable, as the underground root is eaten. So radish is the odd one out, option B. Classification questions of this type depend on the plant part eaten, so tomato (fruit), brinjal (fruit) and lady finger (fruit pod) group together, while the root stands apart. This is the usual basis used in such questions.

subject: Logical Reasoning
concept: Number series with multiplier plus one
explanation:
Look at the ratio pattern. Each term = previous × (position index) + 1:
- 6 × 1 + 1 = 7
- 7 × 2 + 1 = 15
- 15 × 3 + 1 = 46
- 46 × 4 + 1 = 185
- 185 × 5 + 1 = 926
The next number is 926, option C.

subject: Logical Reasoning
explanation:
The person starts facing East. A left turn from East points him North, so he walks 15 m North. A second left turn from North points him West. At the end he is therefore moving towards the West, option A.
The distances (10 m and 15 m) do not affect the direction. Always track the facing direction after each turn: East, then left gives North, then left again gives West. Drawing a small diagram of the path makes it clear.

subject: Logical Reasoning
explanation:
Orange is a kind of fruit, so the orange circle lies inside the fruit circle. Potato is a vegetable, not a fruit, and has no overlap with either fruit or orange, so it is a separate circle.
Figure B shows a small circle inside a larger one plus a separate circle, which is exactly this relationship. The other figures show overlap or three separate/nested sets.

subject: Logical Reasoning
explanation:
Replace the symbols using the given rules: + means ×, × means −, − means ÷, and ÷ means +.
The expression 288 − 24 ÷ 8 + 3 becomes 288 ÷ 24 + 8 × 3.
- Division and multiplication first: 288 ÷ 24 = 12; 8 × 3 = 24.
- Add: 12 + 24 = 36.
The answer is 36, option A.

subject: Computer Science
keyNote: None of the four options equals Σ(2,4,5,6); the simplified SOP is AB' + BC'. The source key (C, A + B + C') is not equivalent to the function.
explanation:
Write the minterms in binary: 2 = 010, 4 = 100, 5 = 101, 6 = 110.
On the K-map group pairs of adjacent ones:
- 4 and 5 (AB'): A = 1, B = 0.
- 2 and 6 (BC'): B = 1, C = 0.
- 4 and 6 are also adjacent (AC'), but are already covered.
Minimal SOP: F = AB' + BC'.
Check options: A + B + C is 1 for 7 minterms; A'B + AC covers 2, 3, 5, 7, which is wrong; A + B + C' covers six minterms including 0; A'B'C is minterm 1 only. None matches, so the question has no correct option.

subject: Computer Science
explanation:
EPROM must be erased by exposing the chip to ultraviolet light through a quartz window, which erases the whole chip. EEPROM is erased electrically, byte by byte, and can be reprogrammed in-circuit without UV light.
- A: speed is not the key difference.
- C: capacity is not the defining advantage.
- D: both EPROM and EEPROM are non-volatile.
So option B is correct.

subject: Computer Science
keyNote: The source key marks C (2^n), which is the count for a binary counter. A Johnson counter with n flip-flops has 2n states, option B.
explanation:
A Johnson (twisted-ring) counter is a shift register whose inverted last output is fed back to the first input. With n flip-flops it cycles through 2n distinct states, for example a 4-bit Johnson counter has 8 states (0000, 1000, 1100, 1110, 1111, 0111, 0011, 0001).
A plain ring counter has n states and a binary counter has 2^n states. So the answer is 2n, option B.

subject: Computer Science
keyNote: Strictly, CMOS uses complementary enhancement-mode devices; depletion-mode loads are characteristic of NMOS. No option fits perfectly, but CMOS (the key) is the only MOSFET family among sensible choices besides PMOS.
explanation:
Of the options, TTL and ECL are bipolar families, so they use no MOSFETs. PMOS and CMOS are MOS families. CMOS pairs an n-channel and a p-channel MOSFET in a complementary arrangement, and is the family that the key selects.
Strictly speaking, the depletion-plus-enhancement combination is characteristic of NMOS (depletion-mode load with enhancement-mode drivers), and standard CMOS uses enhancement-mode devices of both types. The question is therefore loosely worded, and CMOS is only the best available option.

subject: Computer Science
explanation:
Gray code changes only one bit between consecutive values. This avoids large glitches when a value is read while changing, so it is used in analog-to-digital converters and shaft/rotary position encoders, where a read taken at the transition can differ by at most one step.
- Digital communications and data encryption do not typically rely on Gray code.
- Error detection: Gray code is not an error-detecting code (parity and Hamming codes are).
Hence option C is the best answer.

subject: Computer Science
explanation:
A microcomputer is a small computer built around a microprocessor, designed to be used by one person at a time, such as a personal computer, desktop or laptop. It is smaller and cheaper than minicomputers and mainframes.
- A: mainframes are larger.
- C: corporations use many kinds of systems.
- D: being networked does not define a microcomputer.
So option B is correct.

subject: Computer Science
explanation: The Altair 8800, built by MITS and based on the Intel 8080 microprocessor, was introduced in January 1975, when it was featured on the cover of Popular Electronics. It is widely regarded as the machine that started the personal computer revolution and inspired Bill Gates and Paul Allen to write BASIC for it, which led to Microsoft. So the year is 1975, option B.
